treat.intro: Injury and illness are marked by disruptions in the body’s energy flow. Correcting them with acupuncture and herbs enables the body to heal itself.
c1.p: Stimulating precise points along the body’s meridians helps restore proper energy flow — the way electricity must flow without short circuits.
c2.p: Herbs chosen for their effect on Chi are precisely combined into bags, then brewed at home into a medicinal tea.
c3.p: Each course of care begins with a consultation — reading the pulse, tongue, eyes and nails — followed by an individualized prescription.
badge.title: NCCAOM certified
doc.h2: A family tradition, practiced with care.
doc.p1: Born in Guangzhou, Dr. George Fan Xu comes from three generations of Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners. He began learning in his father’s clinic at 14, then studied for five years at Guangzhou’s Traditional Chinese Medical College under some of the finest specialists in China.
doc.p2: Patients often come to him with chronic problems that have gone unresolved for years. His aim is to treat the whole person and re-establish balance.
brew.p: Chinese herbs are chosen for their effect on the flow of Chi. Traditional Chinese Medicine rarely offers instant relief — it works on the root cause of the illness.
s1.p: Traditional diagnosis leads to an individualized prescription.
s2.p: A precise combination of specific herbs is mixed together into bags.
s3.p: Each bag is boiled down into several cups of “tea,” taken the prescribed number of times per day.
s4.p: Dr. Xu follows up office visits with phone calls to check on your progress.
brew.quote: “Most brews do not taste bad, but they rarely taste good either. Hold your breath and drink it down fast.”
ethic.quote: The barefoot doctor will go barefoot before he will charge more than his patients can afford.
ethic.p: Dr. Xu puts the patient before money. He takes the time to educate patients about their condition and treatment — and considers it a success when a patient no longer needs him.

about.meta.title: About Dr. George Fan Xu, L.Ac., OMD | Shallowford Herbs
about.meta.description: Third-generation Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner from Guangzhou, in Atlanta since 1987.
about.lede: A third-generation practitioner of Traditional Chinese Medicine from Guangzhou, caring for Atlanta patients since 1987.
about.p1: I was born in Guangzhou (formerly Canton), a harbour city in southern China. My family has a long history of Traditional Chinese Medicine, and for three generations has practiced professionally. Growing up in this environment had a profound influence on me. I began learning the practice at age 14. For several years, I was taught by my father at his clinic.
about.p2: At age 18, I left to attend Guangzhou Traditional Chinese Medicine, one of the most prestigious medical colleges in China. Here I stayed for five years, until graduating. During that time I had the opportunity to study up close and extensively with some of the finest specialists from various styles of Chinese Medicine.
about.p3: I came to the United States in 1983, initially staying in Vermont under a student exchange. Although I enjoyed my time there, I did not find the weather especially appealing, so I moved to Atlanta in 1987. I eventually established a Chinese Medical Clinic in Chamblee (north Atlanta) in 1994. Soon after, I was able to set up a second office in Doraville.
about.p4: Generally, people come to my clinic for chronic problems that have been unresolved for several years by Western medicine. They also come for acute conditions and general health concerns. Usually, there is an initial consultation, after which an individualized prescription will be given. Traditional Chinese Medicine is holistic and integrated. My aim is to cure the whole person and re-establish balance. Remember that I am always available for any questions or concerns you may have.

faq.a1: Traditional Chinese Medicine is a comprehensive, holistic medical system that focuses on restoring balance and promoting the natural healing abilities of the body. Shallowford Herbs practitioners use TCM principles—including acupuncture and herbal therapy—to address both symptoms and underlying patterns of imbalance.
faq.q2: How is TCM different from Western medicine?
faq.a2: While Western medicine often targets specific symptoms or diseases, TCM evaluates your overall health—including energy flow (Qi), organ function, lifestyle, and environment—to create a personalized treatment plan.
faq.a3: When provided by a licensed and experienced practitioner, TCM—including acupuncture and tailored herbal therapy—is considered a safe and well-tolerated approach to health care.
faq.q4: Is belief required for TCM to work?
faq.a4: No. TCM and acupuncture activate physiological responses and the body’s innate healing mechanisms, regardless of personal belief.
faq.q5: What services does Shallowford Herbs & Acupuncture offer?
faq.a5: The clinic provides individualized acupuncture and herbal medicine designed to address chronic and acute concerns, support pain management, improve wellness, and re-establish balance throughout the body.
faq.q6: How does acupuncture help the body?
faq.a6: Acupuncture gently stimulates specific points on the body to improve circulation, regulate the nervous system, support immune function, and promote natural pain relief. It works by encouraging the body’s own healing response.
faq.a7: Acupuncture uses very thin, sterile needles and most patients experience minimal sensation. Many report feeling relaxed during and after treatment.
faq.q8: Do you use Chinese herbal medicine?
faq.a8: Yes. Herbal formulas are prescribed based on a thorough evaluation of your unique constitution and current condition. Herbs are blended to support the body’s balance and energy flow, often alongside acupuncture.
faq.q9: What should I expect during my first visit?
faq.a9: Your first visit includes a detailed health consultation and assessment to understand your unique needs, followed by a treatment plan that may include acupuncture, herbs, or other supportive recommendations.
faq.a10: Absolutely. Treatments are created for each patient based on a detailed assessment that may include diagnostic observation and discussion of your health history, symptom patterns, and wellness goals.
faq.a11: Patients seek care for a wide range of concerns, including unresolved chronic conditions, pain, stress, digestive issues, sleep disturbances, and general wellness support—especially when conventional treatments have not fully relieved symptoms.
faq.q12: How many sessions will I need?
faq.a12: The number of sessions varies depending on your condition, response to treatment, and overall health goals. Some patients notice improvement early, while others benefit from a structured course of care.
faq.q13: Do I need to change my lifestyle or diet?
faq.a13: Personalized lifestyle and dietary guidance may be offered to support your treatment and long-term health, but recommendations are practical and based on your individual habits and wellness goals.
